correctness.rationale: The proof checks every pair type in a 2-thick canonical chain graph. Open twins force the one-omission-per-class condition. Two explicit constant-difference witnesses prove the endpoint obstructions. For sufficiency, selected landmarks exist in every class and the nested distance values \(1,2,3\) give unequal differences except precisely at those endpoints. Inclusion-exclusion then yields the polynomial. The standalone verifier checks the literal definition, coefficient vector, minimum, and basis count for every canonical profile through order \(12\).

value.rationale: The result identifies a sharp structural boundary for a classical distance-localization invariant: in a natural 2-thick multi-level chain graph, all additional double-resolution failures collapse to two endpoint events. This yields a complete all-set classification, exact polynomial, exact minimum, and exact basis count. The endpoint phenomenon is not a mere restatement of the ordinary twin-class condition and is relevant to enumeration and sensor-placement questions with an unknown additive timing offset.
